publicTopic.how-it-works.section1.title: 1 · Your device is authoritative
publicTopic.how-it-works.section1.body: Period history, observations, preferences and local intelligence live in the encrypted Sreadya vault on this device.
publicTopic.how-it-works.section2.title: 2 · Intelligence stays local
publicTopic.how-it-works.section2.body: Prediction v1, insights, reminder planning, reports and the deterministic assistant use local health history rather than sending reproductive-health plaintext to analytics or a cloud AI service.
publicTopic.how-it-works.section3.title: 3 · Continuity is optional
publicTopic.how-it-works.section3.body: When an approved identity/sync service is configured, clients encrypt health content before synchronization. Account-free Sreadya remains complete without that service.
publicTopic.how-it-works.intro: Sreadya separates your local health experience from optional continuity. Tracking, predictions, insights and reports run on the client; account services never become the health-intelligence engine.
publicTopic.cycle-tracking.section1.body: Start or end a period, backdate or correct dates, and delete mistakes from the encrypted local record.
publicTopic.cycle-tracking.section2.body: Record spotting, light, medium or heavy flow and add optional private cycle notes or reproductive observations.
publicTopic.cycle-tracking.section3.body: Use monthly, timeline and year views to review the history you entered. Historical editing remains available.
publicTopic.cycle-tracking.intro: Sreadya supports period start/end, corrections, flow, notes, month/timeline/year history, irregular cycles and cycle statistics without forcing a 28-day assumption.
publicTopic.predictions.section1.title: Expected date and window
publicTopic.predictions.section1.body: See the most likely next-period date, a wider expected window, confidence and cycle-length trend.
publicTopic.predictions.section2.title: History and accuracy
publicTopic.predictions.section2.body: The browser stores prediction history locally with the algorithm version and input reference so later outcomes can be evaluated.
publicTopic.predictions.section3.title: Fertility boundary
publicTopic.predictions.section3.body: Ovulation and fertile-window estimates appear only where enabled by life-stage context. They are not certified contraception or a clinical fertility guarantee.
publicTopic.predictions.intro: Predictions are estimates from your own valid cycle history. Sreadya shows uncertainty and confidence instead of pretending future biology is certain.
publicTopic.reminders.section1.title: Private default
publicTopic.reminders.section1.body: New local vaults enable the discreet 3-day cycle reminder by default. Seven-day, one-day, expected-day and late reminders remain adjustable.
publicTopic.reminders.section2.title: Personal reminder families
publicTopic.reminders.section2.body: Create medication, contraception-context, supplement, ovulation-test, pregnancy-test or custom wellness reminders and choose a snooze interval.
publicTopic.reminders.section3.title: Browser-adapted delivery
publicTopic.reminders.section3.body: Reminder Health shows permission, time zone, installed-PWA state and the next intent. Closed-app delivery is only claimed when the browser and reviewed delivery path can provide it.
publicTopic.reminders.intro: A private 3-day-before-period reminder is the frozen default. You can change cycle reminders, personal reminder families, time, quiet hours, snooze and notification privacy.
publicTopic.insights.section1.title: Cycle statistics
publicTopic.insights.section1.body: Average, shortest and longest cycle, period duration and variation are calculated from your own valid history.
publicTopic.insights.section2.title: Patterns you recorded
publicTopic.insights.section2.body: Review flow, symptom, PMS, mood, pain and sleep patterns when enough local observations exist.
publicTopic.insights.section3.title: Prediction accuracy
publicTopic.insights.section3.body: When actual period outcomes exist, Sreadya can evaluate historical prediction accuracy without turning the result into a medical explanation.
publicTopic.insights.intro: Insights summarize your records; they do not invent diagnoses. Sreadya explains the data range and sources behind an observation.
publicTopic.life-stages.section1.title: Change context without deleting history
publicTopic.life-stages.section1.body: Changing life-stage mode changes presentation and relevant estimates; it never erases health history you already recorded.
publicTopic.life-stages.section2.title: Trying to conceive
publicTopic.life-stages.section2.body: Optional fertility-oriented estimates can be shown in this context while keeping the non-contraceptive and non-diagnostic boundary explicit.
publicTopic.life-stages.section3.title: Your mode is private
publicTopic.life-stages.section3.body: Life-stage settings are stored in the encrypted local Sreadya vault and do not require an account.
publicTopic.life-stages.intro: Sreadya adapts context across regular cycles, trying to conceive, pregnancy, postpartum, breastfeeding, perimenopause, menopause transition and hormonal contraception.
publicTopic.doctor-reports.section1.body: Select dates and categories such as periods, flow, symptoms, pain, temperature/ovulation observations and optional notes.
publicTopic.doctor-reports.section2.body: Sensitive categories are not silently added. The preview is generated locally before CSV or PDF export becomes available.
publicTopic.doctor-reports.section3.body: Sreadya does not upload the report to create it. Export is an explicit user action.
publicTopic.doctor-reports.intro: A report exists only after you choose a date range and categories, preview the result, and explicitly export it.
publicTopic.privacy.section1.title: Encrypted local vault
publicTopic.privacy.section1.body: Health records are encrypted before IndexedDB persistence. The browser-local vault remains authoritative.
publicTopic.privacy.section2.title: PIN and platform boundaries
publicTopic.privacy.section2.body: Web supports a local PIN gate and automatic lock. Sreadya does not rename that into native biometric security, and the browser controls screenshots and app-switcher previews.
publicTopic.privacy.section3.title: Review and revoke
publicTopic.privacy.section3.body: The Privacy Center links backup/export, connected-device state, partner sharing, notification privacy, account boundaries and sanitized diagnostics.
publicTopic.privacy.intro: Privacy is an operating rule: account-free equality, encrypted local storage, no reproductive-health analytics payload and truthful platform limitations.
publicTopic.security.section1.title: Local cryptography
publicTopic.security.section1.body: Health records use authenticated encryption. Backup restore validates integrity and compatibility before replacing live health data.
publicTopic.security.section2.title: Optional E2EE continuity
publicTopic.security.section2.body: The sync protocol transports authenticated ciphertext and operational metadata; the service is not supposed to receive readable health content.
publicTopic.security.section3.title: Responsible reporting
publicTopic.security.section3.body: Security reports should contain technical reproduction information, not exported health records.
publicTopic.security.intro: Sreadya fails closed around keys, health plaintext and release evidence. Security boundaries are separate for the local vault, optional continuity and software delivery.
publicTopic.sync.section1.title: Local-first during outage or absence
publicTopic.sync.section1.body: Logging and local intelligence keep working. The Web client reports the continuity endpoint state instead of simulating a successful server sync.
publicTopic.sync.section2.title: Ciphertext-only service boundary
publicTopic.sync.section2.body: When continuity is configured, clients encrypt locally and the service stores opaque ciphertext plus minimum operational metadata.
publicTopic.sync.section3.title: Trusted devices and recovery
publicTopic.sync.section3.body: Device enrollment, revocation, passkey identity and recovery require the optional continuity service and authenticated device state. They are never faked by the static site.
publicTopic.sync.intro: Cross-device continuity is optional. The static GitHub Pages client remains fully usable account-free even when no approved sync-service URL is configured.
publicTopic.sync.boundary: Provider-dependent continuity is part of the approved target architecture but is not claimed as live on a static Pages deployment without a configured service endpoint.
publicTopic.accessibility.section1.title: Presentation choices
publicTopic.accessibility.section1.body: Choose larger text, reduced motion, high contrast, light/dark appearance and easy-language guidance. Preferences remain local to this browser.
publicTopic.accessibility.section2.title: Worldwide formatting
publicTopic.accessibility.section2.body: Choose metric/imperial units, 12/24-hour time and a BCP-47 formatting locale. RTL direction is applied for supported right-to-left locales while the reviewed message catalogue remains English.
publicTopic.accessibility.section3.title: Offline and small-screen use
publicTopic.accessibility.section3.body: The installable PWA keeps an offline application shell and the private navigation is designed for desktop, tablet and one-handed mobile layouts.
publicTopic.accessibility.intro: Sreadya provides light/dark presentation, text scaling, reduced motion, high contrast, keyboard/screen-reader semantics, easy-language guidance and locale/RTL formatting infrastructure.
publicTopic.download.section1.title: Web / PWA · available now
publicTopic.download.section1.body: Open the full account-free Web client in a browser or install it to the Home Screen/Desktop for a focused standalone experience.
publicTopic.download.section2.title: Android
publicTopic.download.section2.body: The Android client is built from the same capability contract. Until a production store/download channel is published, use reviewed Android/PWA guidance rather than an unverified package link.
publicTopic.download.section3.title: iPhone / iPad
publicTopic.download.section3.body: Native iOS distribution is shown only when available. The reviewed Safari Add to Home Screen path provides the current installable Web option.
publicTopic.download.intro: Choose the Sreadya client that is actually available. This static site does not invent an App Store or Play Store listing that has not been published.
publicTopic.help.section1.title: I want to back up or restore
publicTopic.help.section1.body: Use CycleVault to create a user-chosen encrypted backup and validate it before restore.
publicTopic.help.section2.title: I want to understand privacy
publicTopic.help.section2.body: The Privacy Center shows health-data location, local encryption, notification privacy, partner access, devices and diagnostics.
publicTopic.help.section3.title: Something technical is wrong
publicTopic.help.section3.body: Generate a sanitized diagnostics preview. It intentionally excludes period dates, symptoms, notes, sexual activity and fertility/pregnancy payloads.
publicTopic.help.intro: Start with the task you need. Sreadya keeps recovery, privacy and health actions explicit rather than hiding them behind a generic support form.
publicTopic.about.section1.title: One product contract
publicTopic.about.section1.body: Cycle semantics, prediction rules, reminder meaning, privacy boundaries, schemas and crypto/sync formats are shared across clients.
publicTopic.about.section2.title: No-account equality
publicTopic.about.section2.body: Core tracking, logging, predictions, insights, reminders, reports, privacy and local vault features do not require an account.
publicTopic.about.section3.title: Health boundaries
publicTopic.about.section3.body: Sreadya supports personal tracking and estimates but does not silently turn them into diagnosis, treatment or certified contraception claims.
publicTopic.about.intro: Sreadya is one privacy-first cycle and wellness companion across Android, iOS and Web, with platform-specific adapters but one health-data meaning.
publicTopic.release-notes.section1.title: Complete navigation
publicTopic.release-notes.section1.body: The More hub and public capability catalogue expose the launch contract instead of leaving secondary routes hidden.
publicTopic.release-notes.section2.title: Product-depth closure
publicTopic.release-notes.section2.body: Structured logging, prediction history, personal reminders, privacy/app-lock, diagnostics and explicit account/sync states are integrated into the Web product.
publicTopic.release-notes.section3.title: Fail-closed release evidence
publicTopic.release-notes.section3.body: Web source is scanned for backlog markers and the product-completeness gate checks 258 launch IDs plus deeper user-story surfaces.
publicTopic.release-notes.intro: The current Web release focuses on complete feature discovery, structured local workspaces, product-depth evidence and truthful provider/platform boundaries.
publicTopic.terms.section1.title: Predictions are estimates
publicTopic.terms.section1.body: Expected dates, PMS, ovulation or fertile-window estimates can be uncertain and must not be treated as guarantees.
publicTopic.terms.section2.title: No certified contraception claim
publicTopic.terms.section2.body: The initial release does not claim contraceptive effectiveness or a certified avoid-pregnancy method.
publicTopic.terms.section3.title: You control exports and sharing
publicTopic.terms.section3.body: Doctor reports, partner summaries and diagnostics require explicit user actions and have separate scopes.
publicTopic.terms.intro: Sreadya is a personal tracking and wellness product. Its estimates and observations are not a substitute for professional medical diagnosis, treatment or emergency care.
publicTopic.security.report.section1.bod: Describe the affected route/version, browser or device, reproducible technical steps and observed security impact.
publicTopic.security.report.section2.bod: Do not share vault keys, recovery secrets, passphrases or real health payloads in a security report.
publicTopic.security.report.section3.bod: Use synthetic values when a reproduction needs example data. Sreadya diagnostics are designed around allowlisted technical state.
publicTopic.security.report.intro: Report security issues with the minimum technical information needed to reproduce the problem. Do not attach real menstrual, fertility, pregnancy, sexual-activity or medication records.
publicTopic.security-report.section1.bod: Security reporting guidance lives at the architecture-approved nested route.
publicTopic.security-report.intro: This legacy route is retained for compatibility. The canonical security-reporting page is /security/report.
privacyPolicy.intro: Sreadya Privacy Policy. Account-free Sreadya and account-based Sreadya are equal first-class experiences. Core health tools remain available without an account, while optional end-to-end encrypted continuity adds cross-device convenience without creating a developer-readable reproductive-health database.
privacyPolicy.section1.title: Account-free and local core
privacyPolicy.section1.body: You can use Sreadya without an account. Cycle tracking, logging, predictions, insights, reminders, reports, privacy controls and encrypted backup remain local-first core health features. Disabling sync does not disable local Sreadya.
privacyPolicy.section2.title: Account and encrypted continuity
privacyPolicy.section2.body: If you enable optional continuity, your health content is encrypted before leaving an authorized device. The synchronization service receives ciphertext, wrapped key or recovery material and only the minimum operational metadata needed for account/device authorization and synchronization. Sreadya infrastructure does not possess the health-vault decryption key.
privacyPolicy.section3.title: Minimum operational metadata
privacyPolicy.section3.body: Operational metadata can include opaque account, device, vault, object or event identifiers, ciphertext size, protocol/version counters, synchronization timestamps, public device-verification material, and authorization or revocation state. It does not authorize the service to receive readable period dates, symptoms, sexual activity, fertility observations, pregnancy state, medication details, private notes, prediction inputs or report contents.
privacyPolicy.section4.title: Account recovery and trusted devices
privacyPolicy.section4.body: Account access and old-vault decryption are separate. Where a release enables verified email or SMS recovery, email or SMS can help recover account identity but cannot by itself decrypt the old health vault. A trusted device can approve a new device, while the independent recovery key can restore vault continuity. Losing every trusted device and the recovery key can make the previous vault unrecoverable.
privacyPolicy.section5.title: Retention and deletion
privacyPolicy.section5.body: Local records remain until you edit or delete them, wipe Sreadya data, uninstall the client, or replace them with a validated restore. Account deletion removes server-side account and synchronized ciphertext state controlled by Sreadya. Sreadya cannot remotely erase former device copies, screenshots, user-created export files, CycleVault backups or data already sent to another destination; those copies must be deleted where they are stored.
privacyPolicy.section6.title: Sharing, reports and backups
privacyPolicy.section6.body: Reports, partner summaries, QR codes, CycleVault backups and other exports leave Sreadya only after explicit user action. CycleVault uses a user-held backup passphrase and remains separate from account-continuity recovery.
privacyPolicy.section7.title: Health integrations
privacyPolicy.section7.body: Health Connect and Apple Health are optional, permission-scoped integrations. Their platform stores remain separate systems under their providers’ rules, and permissions can be revoked through the operating system.
privacyPolicy.section8.title: Diagnostics and analytics
privacyPolicy.section8.body: Sreadya does not use advertising SDKs, behavioral analytics, remote session replay or developer health-payload telemetry. Diagnostics are limited to reviewed operational status and must not contain readable reproductive-health payloads.
privacyPolicy.section9.title: Email, SMS and external providers
privacyPolicy.section9.body: Email or SMS verification providers are used only if those channels are enabled for a release. If enabled, they may process contact and delivery metadata under their own terms. App stores, operating systems, notification services, platform health stores and destinations chosen by the user are separate data flows.
privacyPolicy.section10.title: Policy and release truth
privacyPolicy.section10.body: A sync-enabled release must keep this policy, in-product privacy information and applicable store declarations aligned with the exact shipping behavior. Repository tests do not claim that an external store-console submission or production provider account has been completed.
